rows.label: Uses your data for AI or ads

rivals.name: Bearable
rivals.thesis: Bearable is a phone app where you tap to rate symptoms, mood and habits, and it backs your data up to its own servers. Glyph Well lets you say how your day went on a Mac or iPhone and keeps every entry as a line in a file in your own vault.
short: Bearable logs by taps on iOS and Android. Well logs by talking, on Mac and iPhone.
Bearable backs data up to servers in Frankfurt. Well keeps it in your vault, with no account.
Bearable puts correlation reports and history past 30 days behind its subscription. Well is free.
rivals.pick: Pick Bearable if you want a mature Android or iPhone tracker with 30+ reports, a large community and a sliding-scale program for people who cannot pay.

price: Free core tracking. Optional subscription $6.99 a month or $34.99 a year
input: Taps: rate symptoms, mood and habits
patterns: Weekly reports and a correlation graph free, correlation reports paid
account: Email and password, needed for backup
training: Does not sell data. Facebook SDK shares anonymised IDs to measure ads
export: Export and delete everything from the app

rivals.note: The homepage says Garmin, Oura and Samsung Health sync is planned, not available today.

rivals.name: Welltory
rivals.thesis: Welltory measures heart rate variability with your phone camera or a smartwatch and turns it into stress and energy scores on its own US servers. Glyph Well records what you say about your day in your own vault and shows how often things followed each other.
short: Welltory centres on heart rate variability. Well centres on your own words, with Garmin and Apple Health beside them.
Welltory needs an account and stores data mainly in the US. Well has no account.
Welltory uses anonymized AI chats to improve its own models and shares ad IDs in the US. Well does neither.
rivals.pick: Pick Welltory if you want detailed heart rate variability and blood pressure analysis from a camera or smartwatch reading, with guided recommendations.

price: Basic features free. Premium $99 a year or $599 lifetime
input: Heart readings by phone camera or smartwatch, plus lifelogging
patterns: Reports such as Stress Impact and Sleep
account: Required: email, Google, Apple or Facebook login
storage: Welltory servers, mainly in the United States
training: Anonymized AI chats improve its own models. US ad sharing with Meta, Google, TikTok, opt-out
export: Export from app settings, JSON or CSV

rivals.note: The plans page mentions a monthly plan but does not list its price.

rivals.name: Guava Health
rivals.alt_title: A free, private Guava Health alternative
rivals.thesis: Guava Health is a cloud health record: you log symptoms and medications, pull in patient portal records and share a summary with your doctor. Glyph Well keeps your log and lab results as files in your own vault and makes the visit summary PDF on your device.
short: Guava keeps your records in its HIPAA-compliant cloud. Well keeps them in your vault.
Guava's AI assistant runs on OpenAI and costs $8 a month. Well is free.
Guava can import patient portal records. Well takes lab results you add yourself.
rivals.pick: Pick Guava Health if you want your patient portal records pulled into one place, on the web as well as phones, and family caregivers on one profile.

price: Free plan. Premium $8 a month or $78 a year
input: Record symptoms, medications and lifestyle. Premium AI can enter data
patterns: Trends and correlations free, automatic insights on Premium
account: Email address to manage your account
training: Not used for ads. Processed by OpenAI. AI training not stated
export: Full download on request by email, within 30 days

rivals.name: Exist
rivals.thesis: Exist pulls data from services like Apple Health, Garmin and Oura into its own servers, adds mood and tags you enter, and finds correlations. Glyph Well reads Garmin and Apple Health beside the words you speak and keeps all of it in your own vault.
short: Exist costs $6.99 a month after a 30-day trial. Well is free.
Exist logs by scores and tags. Well logs by talking.
Exist keeps your data on its hosted servers with an account. Well has no account.
rivals.pick: Pick Exist if you want many services synced in one place (Garmin, Oura, Withings, Strava, calendar and more), a web app, and experiments to test a hunch.

price: $6.99 a month or $62.90 a year, 30-day free trial
input: Synced services plus manual scores, tags and mood
storage: Exist servers hosted outside the United States
training: Never sells data. AI training not stated
export: Export from the account page or the API

rivals.note: Exist says it will not add large language models and uses statistical methods.
